entries.ff74e43acc09ee9c: A business that manufactures and sells silicon wafers for semiconductor manufacturers, and the group's only reportable segment. Silicon wafers serve as the substrate material when semiconductor manufacturers make semiconductors such as memory and logic chips. Wafer diameters have grown generation by generation from 100 mm to 125 mm, 150 mm, 200 mm and 300 mm, and the company produces polished wafers, finished to a mirror surface, and epitaxial wafers, which have a thin single-crystal silicon layer on their surface. Production involves two steps: pulling single-crystal ingots from polycrystalline silicon melted in quartz crucibles, and then slicing the ingots thin and grinding, polishing and cleaning them in the wafer processing step. 300 mm wafers are manufactured in Imari City and Kohoku Town in Saga Prefecture, Yonezawa City in Yamagata Prefecture, Omura City in Nagasaki Prefecture, and Taiwan; wafers of 200 mm and smaller are manufactured at locations across Japan, as well as in the United States, Indonesia and Taiwan. Polycrystalline silicon for semiconductors is manufactured in Yokkaichi City, Mie Prefecture, and in the United States. Revenue for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥409,670 million, and the largest customer was Sumitomo Corporation (revenue of ¥110,600 million, 27.0% of the total). In the fiscal year ended December 2025, demand for advanced 300 mm wafers for AI semiconductors was strong, while shipments of 200 mm and smaller wafers remained weak.
